tip:
before you trust an AI answer, ask it: "what would make this answer wrong?"
you'll catch more mistakes than you think.

stop asking AI to "make this better".
paste your draft and ask: "list the weakest sentences and rewrite only those".

give AI one example of what good looks like.
one example beats ten adjectives.

end your prompt with: "ask me 3 questions before you start."
the answer gets twice as specific.

long PDF? ask AI for the 5 decisions it asks you to make, not a summary.
much more useful.

tell AI who the reader is.
"explain this to a busy client" beats "explain this" every time.

turn AI into a tough reviewer:
"you're a skeptical expert. find the 3 biggest holes in this plan."

learning something new? ask AI to quiz you instead of explaining.
you remember what you retrieve, not what you read.

messy voice memo -> clear plan:
record your thoughts, paste the transcript, ask for "next 3 actions with owners".

before a hard conversation, use voice mode:
"play my manager, push back on my raise request, don't go easy."

AI wrote something generic?
give it 3 of your old texts and say "match this voice".

when AI gets it wrong, don't start over.
say exactly what's off and ask for one change at a time.
comparing products or plans? ask AI for a table with the trade-offs, then ask what it would pick and why.

the most useful prompt for decisions:
"imagine this failed in 6 months. what went wrong?"

save your best prompts in a note.
the people getting the most from AI aren't smarter, they reuse what works.

stuck on an email? paste it and ask:
"what will the reader feel? make it clearer and kinder in half the words."
